newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate at 5.5 pct on high liquidity.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate at 5.5 pct on high liquidity.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate stayed at 5.5 percent on Tuesday as the market remained flush, dealers said.
They said the rate was also pressured by persistent lending by foreign banks which have excess funds.
"Generally, the market is still long. The foreign banks, in particular, are holding lots of money," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Earlier, one-week money was at 6.30/80 percent against 6.70/80 on Monday.
One-month money was at 7.35/40 percent from 7.40, and three-month at 7.45/50 percent against 7.50/55.
Dealers said they expected interbank rates to hover around current levels though rates could firm slightly on Wednesday due to payment for Bank Negara bills worth one billion ringgit.

The central bank earlier announced that it accepted bids at an average yield of 6.353 percent at the auction of 30-day bills amounting to 500 million ringgit, against 6.771 percent at the previous auction on June 10. Bank Negara also accepted bids for 91-day bills for 500 million ringgit at an average yield of 6.371 percent against 6.461 percent previously.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were up across the board as short-term interbank rates continued their softening trend.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up five points to 92.68, or an implied yield of 7.32 percent.
The December contract rose four to 92.78, or 7.22 percent while March 1998 was up five to 92.80, or 7.20 percent.
